meta.title: Step 32 — Employee Turnover Evaluation
meta.subtitle: Explore the model's predictions for 594 employees, understand its mistakes and see the factors behind individual predictions.
meta.unobtrusive_note: Retrospective holdout evaluation — results describe performance on the previously evaluated dataset.

metric_explanations.employees_evaluated: Total number of retrospective employee holdout cases evaluated.
metric_explanations.accuracy: How many predictions were correct overall across both stayers and leavers.
metric_explanations.precision: Of the employees predicted to leave, how many actually left (low false alarm rate).
metric_explanations.recall: Of the employees who actually left, how many the model successfully identified.
metric_explanations.f1_score: A balanced harmonic mean combining precision and recall into a single metric.
metric_explanations.roc_auc: How well the model separates employees who left from those who stayed across thresholds.
metric_explanations.pr_auc: Precision-recall curve area showing retention detection quality under class imbalance.
metric_explanations.total_errors: Total prediction errors across the cohort (False Positives + False Negatives).

high_risk.label: High Risk
high_risk.description: High turnover flight risk requiring prioritized HR engagement.

medium_risk.label: Medium Risk
medium_risk.description: Elevated flight probability exceeding the 0.361 decision threshold.

low_risk.label: Low Risk
low_risk.description: Healthy organizational retention anchors and low turnover risk.

risk_distribution.disclaimer: These three bands are dashboard categories and are not independently validated HR intervention thresholds. Model scores serve as decision-support information and do not guarantee future actions.

global_shap.title: What factors influence the model overall?
global_shap.subtitle: Global SHAP feature importance ranking across all 594 evaluated employees.
global_shap.interpretation: Global feature importance shows which variables have the largest overall impact on model risk scores across the cohort. Higher values indicate stronger influence on predictions, but do not imply real-world causality.
global_shap.disclaimer: SHAP feature importance reflects statistical model attribution within the trained architecture; it does not prove that changing an attribute will prevent turnover.
